learnerPresentation.initialPresentation: A 56-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes presents with an 8-month history of progressive left shoulder stiffness. The shoulder was initially very painful, especially at night, but the pain has reduced slightly. Stiffness is now the dominant problem. She struggles to reach behind her back, reach across her body, dress normally, and sleep comfortably. There was no trauma or dislocation. She previously attended physiotherapy elsewhere, mainly involving deep tissue massage, but she reports no meaningful improvement. She is frustrated and asks, “Will this ever get better?”
